capability: Map every part and link before moving a folder
title: Map the joins, then merge.

hook.picture: Close: the whale drags a small folder, a short line of six cards, onto a bigger line. On the drop, threads between the cards stretch.
hook.words: Just merge it. It will be fine.

problem_in_viewer_words.body: I merged the folder and half the links point nowhere.
problem_in_viewer_words.who: an engineer after a Friday repo merge

why_it_keeps_happening.picture: Pull back: folders moved by hand across a big codebase. Three times, every 2 beats, then 1, then half, a move leaves loose thread ends where links used to land.
why_it_keeps_happening.words: Nobody knows which parts depend on which.

stakes.body: Broken imports and dead links ship, and a weekend goes to tracing them by hand.

solution_hint: Draw each link before you move a thing.

metaphor.body: A folder is a row of cards tied by threads. Mapping draws every thread as a checked join before anything moves, so a thread with no far end is caught on the map.

steps.picture: Before any drag, the whale reads the folder: each part becomes a card, each link a dashed join drawn between two cards. Six cards, four joins.
steps.words: Draw each link before you move a thing.
steps.sound: Two tones per join, struck as it is drawn.

steps.picture: Each join is checked: does the far end exist? Four joins resolve and turn teal; the whale rings each one.
steps.words: Each link is checked. Does it land?
steps.sound: Four unison pairs, one per teal join.

steps.picture: Push-in: on a second folder, one join's far end is empty. It glows raw sienna and a flag stands on it, before any move happens.
steps.words: Broken before the move, not after.
steps.sound: The pair beats against an empty end.

steps.picture: The map settles beside the folder as a small lattice, saved to reuse on the next folder. A label slides onto a join: seam.
steps.words: Each checked link is a seam.

real_case.claim: sheaf-port builds a typed index of a folder's parts and links. Its sanity check prints 6 parts and 4 teal links, and it caps at 120 parts. It does not decide merge safety.

honest_limit.picture: Push to a merged line: every join is teal, yet a pod runs the merged code and answers ✕. The links land, but on cards from the wrong version.
honest_limit.words: Every link landed. The merge still broke.

not_this.body: A clean map is not a safe merge.

ending_pattern.body: The same drop as the cold open, made after the map: the one bad join is fixed first, the folder lands, and every thread holds.
ending_pattern.callback: The drop that snapped four threads in bar 1 repeats in the same framing, and every thread holds.

end_belief.body: Map the links first. Then decide to merge.
